newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Six killed in New Zealand shooting rampage.
newsitem.headline: Six killed in New Zealand shooting rampage.

text.p: New Zealand police said six people were shot dead and up to five were seriously wounded on Saturday when a gunman went on a shooting rampage in a central North Island town.

The shootings occurred around 9.00 a.m. (2000 GMT Friday) in the small town of Raurimu, which lies near Mount Ruapehu, an active volcano. The killer was believed to have been armed with a 12-gauge shotgun.
A police spokesman said police were searching dense bush near the scene for the possibility of more victims.
"A scene search is underway. There is a possibility of further victims, but that's to be confirmed," he told Reuters.
Police have arrested the suspected gunman, reported to be 50 years old and possibly related to some of the dead and wounded.
Wanganui Acting District Commander Jeff Holloway said police took the suspect into custody shortly before midday (2300 GMT). They were still trying to identify the dead.

"The victims have not yet been properly identified. We don't know all the names as yet. We believe that a number of them at least are residents and may be related to the suspect," he told a news conference.
The wounded were ferried by helicopters to hospitals in the district, he said. Raurimu was evacuated after police were notified of the shooting.
Police said the gunman, believed to be a local resident, was arrested in farmland close to the scene.
Helicopter pilot Guy Beange described the scene as "like Vietnam", with police and helicopters everywhere.
He said the suspect was found in the bush naked and unarmed.
Beange flew one elderly woman with a serious shotgun wound to the back to Palmerston North Hospital at 1.30 p.m. (0030 GMT).
Earlier this morning, a young man was flown to the hospital with a gunshot wound to the head. Two other people were taken to hospital by ambulance, Beange said.
